lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Meal Planning, Cooking, and Food Management
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: leftovers and storage

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic leftovers and storage task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner finds one real leftover food or an open food item already in the household, such as extra cooked rice, a half-used jar of sauce, or cut fruit, chooses a container that actually fits and seals it, writes today's date on it, and places it in the correct storage location (refrigerator, freezer, or pantry) based on what kind of food it is.
safetyNotes: No knife, stove, or hot surface is used in this task; only handling already-cooled or room-temperature food and containers.
If a food item looks or smells spoiled, the learner shows it to a trusted adult and does not taste it to check.

simulationAlternative.description: If no real leftover food is available right now, the learner instead completes the storage-matching exercise on this task sheet, matching each food on the provided list to its correct container type, storage location, and safe timeframe using the storage rules given.

materials: adult-or-local: one real leftover food or open food item from the household
learner-local: a storage container or resealable bag that fits the food

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Was the food already being stored correctly before you checked it, or did you have to fix something? Describe what, if anything, changed.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Storage accuracy: The container fits and seals, the date is written clearly, and the location matches the storage rules for that specific food. | Timeframe reasoning: States a correct safe-use-by date and explains it using the storage rules for that food. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner check two more food items in the household using the same process and compare the three safe-use-by dates, explaining which type of food had the shortest safe window and why.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: leftovers and storage worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner finds one real leftover food or an open food item already in the household, such as extra cooked rice, a half-used jar of sauce, or cut fruit, chooses a container that actually fits and seals it, writes today's date on it, and places it in the correct storage location (refrigerator, freezer, or pantry) based on what kind of food it is.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact leftovers and storage decision or action.
Model move 2: Before storing anything, find and describe your food item.
Model move 3: Using the storage-rules reference, decide on the right container, location, and timeframe for your specific food, then store it.

Model check: Storage accuracy: The container fits and seals, the date is written clearly, and the location matches the storage rules for that specific food. | Timeframe reasoning: States a correct safe-use-by date and explains it using the storage rules for that food.

resources.title: leftovers and storage action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for leftovers and storage.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: leftovers and storage coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner finds one real leftover food or an open food item already in the household, such as extra cooked rice, a half-used jar of sauce, or cut fruit, chooses a container that actually fits and seals it, writes today's date on it, and places it in the correct storage location (refrigerator, freezer, or pantry) based on what kind of food it is.
Coach direction: Before storing anything, find and describe your food item.
Learner prompt: Name the food item you found, how it was left out or stored before now, and roughly how long ago it was prepared or opened.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: leftovers and storage complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Using the storage-rules reference, decide on the right container, location, and timeframe for your specific food, then store it.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I chose a container or bag that seals and actually fits the amount of food.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I wrote today's date clearly on the container or a label attached to it.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I placed the container in the correct location (refrigerator, freezer, or pantry) for that specific food.

Equal-access rule: If no real leftover food is available right now, the learner instead completes the storage-matching exercise on this task sheet, matching each food on the provided list to its correct container type, storage location, and safe timeframe using the storage rules given.

resources.title: leftovers and storage minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Was the food already being stored correctly before you checked it, or did you have to fix something? Describe what, if anything, changed.

Success checks: Storage accuracy: The container fits and seals, the date is written clearly, and the location matches the storage rules for that specific food. | Timeframe reasoning: States a correct safe-use-by date and explains it using the storage rules for that food.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: leftovers and storage supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional leftovers and storage condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Storage accuracy: The container fits and seals, the date is written clearly, and the location matches the storage rules for that specific food. | Timeframe reasoning: States a correct safe-use-by date and explains it using the storage rules for that food..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Storage accuracy: The container fits and seals, the date is written clearly, and the location matches the storage rules for that specific food. | Timeframe reasoning: States a correct safe-use-by date and explains it using the storage rules for that food.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
